options.content:
### Food ordering agent in production
One simulated day = **30 s** by default. Rates use 1-minute windows (about **2 simulated days**). Scenario switches live on the [control panel](http://localhost:8000). Decide A/B tests in the notebook, not here.

panels.title: Completion rate
panels.description: Share of conversations that ended with the user's goal done (order placed, complaint resolved).

panels.title: Judge fail rate
panels.description: LLM-as-judge verdicts on a random 10% sample. The judge itself is imperfect.

panels.title: Refund rate (delayed)
panels.description: Refunds arrive 1-3 simulated days after the order: wait-and-see telemetry.

panels.title: Completion and handoff
panels.description: Implicit feedback: did the conversation reach its goal?

panels.title: User corrections per conversation
panels.description: Implicit feedback: users fixing items, sizes, or restaurants.

panels.title: Judge failures by mode
panels.description: Share of judged conversations flagged, by the failure mode the judge named.

panels.title: Refund rate (delayed label)
panels.description: Refunds show up 1-3 simulated days after the problem.

panels.title: Invariants: checks that need no ground truth
Invariant violations per order
panels.description: Items must exist on the menu, prices must match, discounts must follow policy, allergies must be respected.

panels.title: Discounts granted
panels.description: Dollars per second given away as discounts.

panels.title: Requests flagged as possible prompt injection
panels.description: A heuristic detector. Attackers adapt, so its recall decays.

panels.title: Data drift (Evidently job, PSI against a 2-day reference)
Drift score by column
panels.description: Population stability index; above 0.1 counts as drift.

panels.title: Catalog coverage (nightly)
panels.description: Computed each simulated night from the recommender's logs.

targets.legendFormat: share for restaurants opened this week

panels.title: Order value by prompt version
panels.description: Average value of placed orders. Means only; no confidence intervals here.

panels.title: Shadow release: llm-2026-09 vs production
panels.description: Both models see the same requests; only production's answers reach users. The two discount lines share the left axis, so you can read the gap between them; the shadow model violates discount policy about 3-4x as often. Both use a 5m window (~10 simulated days), because violations are rare enough that the 1m ratio is too noisy to read. Disagreement runs about ten times higher and sits on the right axis. The ShadowModelDiscountViolations alert still uses the 1m rule, so it fires within a minute.

options.content: **Why not decide the A/B test here?** These panels average conversations over sliding windows. The experiment randomizes *users*, so the analysis unit is the user, and you need confidence intervals and a planned sample size. See the notebook.

targets.expr: sum by (llm_version, direction) (rate(agent_llm_tokens_total[1m])) / ignoring(direction) group_left sum by (llm_version) (rate(agent_conversations_total[1m]))

panels.title: LLM cost per order
panels.description: Illustrative prices: $3 per million input tokens, $15 per million output tokens.

panels.title: Drift job: seconds since last run
